basis: Thomas is the probable working father of Roanoke Joseph Glasgow-2573 at74%. The inspected 1877 Campbell original explicitly names Thomas and Rose Glasgo as parents of Jos. Glasgo and records J. Glasgo, Son, as informant. The 1866 cohabitation-register-derived account identifies Joe, Lucy Gilbert and nine children. The younger Joseph’s held 1878 marriage and 1880/1900 Campbell households supply a plausible family continuation, supporting the existing identification of the elder Joseph’s Campbell death. Its conflicting birthplace, age and Unmarried entry remain unresolved. Parent names already appeared in the biography; this is a qualified structured father selection, not newly discovered names or a merger of existing branches.
limitations: The original 1877 entry gives age 80 and a ditto Campbell birthplace, whereas the Roanoke account gives Richmond and the 1870 census age 80 implies about 1790. Its consort column repeats Unmarried rather than naming Lucy. The informant is J. Glasgo, designated Son, without a full forename. The younger Joseph’s1914 certificate clearly names mother Lucy Gilbert, but its father abbreviation remains ambiguous Jas./Jos.; independent readings prefer Jas., and the father’s birthplace is uncertain, tentatively Fredericktown, Md. It does not resolve the 1877 deceased’s identity or name Thomas. Census and marriage household accounts are reused captures, not freshly inspected images. Companion death indexes concern the same event. No existing numbered Thomas, marriage to Rose, older Glasgow lineage or common Y-DNA origin is established.
scope: 74% rates the full proposition that the Roanoke family’s Joseph had the Thomas named in this particular Campbell death entry as father. The indexed father role is explicit; the match of the deceased to the Roanoke man is inferred. Thomas’s identity remains on HOLD, with no birth/death dates or birthplace assigned and no WikiTree creation/save authorized by this local selection.
